essence: The mudrā-procedure praised in guru-scripture is now taught.
Mudrā is reflection-natured: on hearing bimba-rise, it is discerned from two predicates.
Emerge-from-bimba defines reflection; that emergence is its instrumentality.
Delight as own-nature-gain, through the body-gate of selves, grants at night — the mudrā of scripture.
Chief is Khecarī, deity-natured in undivided state; as Triśūlinī in the divided.
Karaṅkiṇī, Krodhanā, Bhairavī, Lelihānikā, Mahāpretā, Yogamudrā, Jvālinī, Kṣobhiṇī, Dhruvā.
Though many, Khecarī alone is sung; the rest are her limbs — Padmā and others in Mālinī doctrine.
Their abundance is not detailed here; wherever the Khecarī-absorbed yogī resorts.
That suffices for the goddess's presence; vain pomp is useless; in the desired rite she is chief.
Mudrā is fourfold: of body, hand, speech, mind.
I describe Khecarī fully: seated in lotus, the yogī casts the navel-ether-lord.
Lead the staff-form to the three cavities; held there, drive it swiftly through the three.
Bound in the sky it moves; so Pūrva-śāsana says; mind resting on sound-light-wind and above.
By this practice-yoga, piercing Śiva, one goes supreme; hands below the clavicle, left foot on right.
Open the mouth with little fingers, middle fingers at the nose; ring finger crooks, two index fingers bend the brow.
Tongue and mantrin move, causing the hāhā sound; by trident-practice, Brahmarandhra is present.
Abandoning the foot, one leaves earth instantly; in void and non-void dissolution, one-staff blue-fire.
Bound to three śaktis, three presiding deities, the trident: by this the wise fly in the sky.
Abandoning sky-nature, present as mere existence; trident made equal-taste, standing like taste in taste.
Knowing one-staff, trident sky-going: bind Khecarī mudrā, meditate self and Bhairava.
Joined to Khecarī-cakra, one leaves earth at once — abandoned-portion, conductless, world-abandoned.
Avadhūta, conductless, meditating 'not I', mantra-single-devoted, sees all deities dwelling in the body.
In delight, agitation, egoism, crying, sleep, union, jealousy, form and the rest — in doer, deed, instrument.
Thinking 'not I', contemplating unified, he sees the deity-group dwelling in ear, eye, mouth, nose, cakra.
Ever seeing the grasper, he succeeds by Khecarī; the doubter of vidyā, mala, or scripture fails.
Śiva the sun, Śiva the fire: being cooker, he is priest; the indwelling deities illumine all the world.
Opening the mouth with little finger, brows with index; ring finger, middle in mouth, tongue to palate.
This is goddess Karaṅkiṇī; now hear Jvālinī: jaw and forehead, hands with spread fingers.
Move by wind-force, brow bent inward; open the mouth, tongue out, cause the hāhā sound.
This Jvālinī in the fire-wheel; if one recites her a hundred-and-eight, the three worlds succeed.
See self in other bodies, other from one's own; see movement, gain and loss in the coming-going place.
Dwelling in nine holes and one, roaring, pervading, fixed — this is the sky-goer's yoga-movement.
Binding Kulakuṇḍalinī, unconscious in the atom; the left this one, intent on withdrawal from the universe.
Attaining satisfaction in one's own place, made of knowledge-nectar-taste, go to the Kanda abode, sound made soundless.
While living, the quadrangular body-support is desired; arousing her, knowing the movement progressively come.
Both wheels bound, supporting the branch-ends; from the root place tear the knot of darkness.
Called Vajra, knowledge-born; from both branch-ends, from the triangle's centre, penetrate the liṅga-root.
By the wheels' pair, unity shines; by reversal, throwing off twofold-condition, one moves thence.
From thigh to big toe she throws the fire of time, moving in coming and going, marked by the liṅga.
By their union he grants opening; the knower succeeds in receiving and emitting sap.
This union-wave-opening is supreme; this succession, then another beyond succession — Khecarī supreme.
Called yoni-support, called trident-root; letters dissolve there, into the letterless within the letter-formed.
Uttering to nāda's end, the Kaula-lord body-resembling; occupying the first wheel in the sky, foot pressed on the machine.
Nāda is śakti with true-womb; from true-womb the Kaulinī-abode; by five-seed circle, by trident-piercing order.
Piercing heart-trident-knot, some Rudra-śakti awakens; the wind-wheel place called bindu, the navel-maṇḍala.
Come to Lambikā's place from the twelve-thread exit; by reversing the moon-wheel, enter the body-cage.
She plays dwelling in the māyā-cage; creation and dissolution are again done by Khecarī.
This Vīrāvalī-yoga is the Khecarī-procedure; by kissing form by mouth, hear the supreme principle.
Swallowing the universe in the moon-sun-pot, one becomes sky-goer — the venerable Kāmika.
Releasing Bhava, the bonds-mudrā melts the śaktis; chief of them is Khecarī, by threefold utterance.
The three-head-mudgara goddess is recited bodily; of them two eyes, heart, and the two breasts.
Two testicles and liṅga; having obtained the body, gone — ascertain Bhava's abode and non-Bhava's by utterance.
Mental this; the others, Padmā and eight mudrikās, in Mātṛ-vyūha-kula, are hers and her attendants.
The entire body is the supreme letter's form; this mudrā is Bhairava's mahāmudrā in the cave.
Well-seated in lotus, by fingertip rays suddenly risen and turned back, one dwells by the back.
Inner-standing Khecarī is called contraction, moon-marked; raise the arms and bend.
In the sky, from standing, the sky-called Khecarī is held; from two fists' union in the heart, the heart-mudrā.
Called peace, two hands up and down standing risen; seen with equal gaze, hands joined outside.
This is śakti-mudrā if the hands run downward; of ten fingers after binding the fist.
Khecarī throws the goddess, holding the five-Kuṇḍalinī; dissolution-mudrā if thrown upward.
Exit-mudrā instantly cuts the bound being's bond; in the chasm far off, as if dropping one's self.
By sudden entry the two hands are contracted; downward-looking-natured, with proper gaze.
Called Vīra-Bhairava Khecarī, consciousness-increasing; eightfold in Bhargāṣṭaka-śikhā-kula.
Resorting to many varieties, one stands alone — venerable Khecarī; absorbed in her, one attains the supreme seed.
One seed of manifestation, whose vigor pervades all mantras; one mudrā Khecarī animates the multitude.
Whatever form shines in the Khecarī-cakra's establishment, that is the mudrā; the rest are bodily modification.
At sacrifice's beginning, middle, end; in reflection on knowledge and yoga, in ending obstacles, cutting bonds — the mudrā's proper time.
Penetration into consciousness, presence with unity, dismissal, movement to essential nature, destroying doubts, splendor of cakra-rise — the purpose in order.
Thus the mudrā-procedure, very secret and fruit-giving, is spoken.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta (wonder) with śānta weight (the seal that awakens Khecarī; rest in the sealed form)
rasa.justification: The ahnika teaches the mudrās as seals that awaken Khecarī and melt bonds; wonder at the seal crowns the practice, and the sealed form rests.

sections.SUMMARY: The ahnika teaches the mudrā-vidhi: mudrā as reflection, Khecarī as principal seal with ten forms, the full Khecarī procedure through body, breath and mind, and the eight derived mudrikās; proper time and purpose close the rite.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes mudrā-vidhi: mudrā as reflection-natured, Khecarī as principal seal with ten forms, the full Khecarī procedure through body, breath and mind, and the eight derived mudrikās; proper time and purpose close the rite.
sections.KEY TERMS: mudrā (seal), Khecarī (sky-goer, principal), bimbodaya (twofold predicate), pratibimba (reflection), Devyāyāmala (source), padmāsana (lotus seat), triśūla (trident), Kulakuṇḍalinī, Kanda, nāda, śakti, Kaula, mahāmudrā, Vīra-Bhairava, saṃhāra, utkrāmaṇī, samaya (proper time)
